papers.title: Can Language Models See the Circuit in Pixelated RFIC Passives?
papers.abstract: The emergence of inverse-designed, pixelated passives for microwave and millimeter-wave applications has been a major development in the field of RFIC design. These devices, which appear to be QR-code-like in structure, exist in a generalizable, high-dimensional design space that includes conventional passive topologies. However, these structures are naturally unintuitive for designers, and failures or deviations in performance are difficult to debug. In this work, we ask whether a frontier language model can understand, predict, and edit the responses and layout structure of pixelated passives. The agent, run with all tools disabled, is first asked to read layouts on 18x18 and 27x27 tile grids and, in a single reply, predict the input impedance and loss of the structure from 20-100 GHz. On eight GA-synthesized layouts and five random fills, the predicted Smith-chart locus follows full-wave simulation results closely, with a systematic shift that places features about 16% lower in frequency than EM. On multipath loop structures it identifies notches successfully but shows a smaller frequency bias, about half that of an ideal transmission-line model that ignores bends. The agent is then asked to debug seven designs that fail their specification, and given a budget of five EM simulations and at most twelve changed tiles, it is able to improve all seven and bring five designs within specification. These experiments suggest language models can serve as an interpretability and debugging tool for traditionally non-intuitive inverse-designed passives.

papers.title: A unified geometric design framework for kirigami structures
papers.abstract: Kirigami turns a thin sheet with cuts into a shape-morphing mechanical metamaterial, with applications across science and engineering. While various two- and three-dimensional kirigami design methods have been developed, most of them are only applicable to a limited class of kirigami structures. In this work, we present a unified geometric design framework for kirigami structures. Since the states of a kirigami pattern differ only in which tile corners coincide, one tessellation routine generates them all, and edge-length equalities couple them. A single constrained optimization then designs 2D-to-2D, 2D-to-3D, and 3D-to-3D shape-morphing, compact reconfigurable, and rigidly deployable structures, and one sheet that deploys into two prescribed shapes. The designs further reveal geometric laws hidden in the kirigami mechanism, which explain how reconfiguration transposes the shape of a sheet, how one sheet bends into both a bowl and a saddle, and why the outline of a flat sheet limits the curvature it can reach when it closes again. Altogether, our work paves a new way for the design of shape-morphing mechanical metamaterials.

papers.title: A Microwave-Photonics Formulation of the Rydberg-Atom Receiver
papers.abstract: The performance of Rydberg-atom receivers is seldom stated as a radio-frequency (RF) link budget. The receiver is shown to be an intensity-modulated direct-detection analog optical link whose modulator is the laser-driven vapor. The transmission of a warm vapor is derived in closed form by averaging the four-level response over atomic velocities. The conversion gain, noise figure, bandwidth, intercept points, and spurious-free dynamic range follow from this one function. For a weak probe the instantaneous bandwidth is half the width of the transparency window in two-photon detuning. The local-oscillator beat places the second-order intercept near twice the local-oscillator field, so the local oscillator sets the even-order linearity. For a rubidium transition at 17.04 GHz the closed forms agree with a velocity-resolved density-matrix model to 1% for the slope and the intercepts and to 10% for the bandwidth. They underestimate the group delay by a third. The response is tied to atomic constants, and the sensing volume escapes the Chu limit. However, the noise figure of a warm vapor rules it out as a general replacement for an antenna and low-noise amplifier.

papers.title: Parametric excitation of nano-scale spin waves with controlled phase by an open-resonator-type transducer
papers.abstract: Parametric excitation is one of the most effective methods for the excitation of nano-scale spin waves (SW) (or magnons) in magnetic films and nano-waveguides, as this method removes restrictions on the excited wave wavelength imposed by a finite width of the excitation transducer. Especially efficient parametric excitation of SW is achieved if the SW excitation is based on the effect of voltage-controlled magnetic anisotropy (VCMA). However, in a traditional parametric excitation process, the excited propagating waves have an arbitrary phase, which prevents the use of such waves in signal processing applications. Here, we demonstrate that the use of an VCMA transducer in the form of an open resonator with controlled partial reflections of waves at the boundaries allows one to excite SW having only two allowed phase states, controlled by the phase of the parametric pumping and reflections at the transducer boundaries. These reflections, also, lead to a reduced value of the parametric excitation threshold. In addition, micromagnetic simulations reveal the possibility to tune the phase distribution of the excited magnons using static voltage, which could be useful for applications in probabilistic computing.

papers.title: Disentangling Lengthscales in Disordered Fracture
papers.abstract: The interplay between quenched disorder and collective interactions can generate multiple emergent lengthscales in damage processes, yet their roles in determining the strength of heterogeneous materials remain incompletely understood. Here, we develop a coarse-grained description of load redistribution in the two-dimensional random fuse model (RFM) with Weibull-distributed quenched disorder, interpreting shielding in the crack-tip damage density as a consequence of nonlocal current redistribution. Our numerical results distinguish this emergent screening length, identified as the size of the statistical fracture process zone, from the regularizing length in Bazant's established quasibrittle size-effect law (SEL), revealing their distinct disorder dependences, and challenging previous associations of the two. We further uncover a comparable scaling between the SEL and pre-failure crack extension, suggesting the former may instead be more naturally associated with a percolation process of micro-fractures around the crack-tip. These findings disentangle important emergent lengthscales within the RFM, and highlight a candidate physical mechanism for explaining macroscopic size effects in quasibrittle fracture.

papers.title: What Photocurrent Versus Effective Voltage Tells Us About Charge Generation in Organic Solar Cells
papers.abstract: The photocurrent of an organic solar cell is routinely plotted against an effective voltage and used to extract an exciton dissociation probability, and through it a free-charge generation efficiency. The photocurrent measures neither. Using a drift-diffusion model in which free-charge generation is field independent and losses occur only by bimolecular recombination, we show that the apparent dissociation probability returned by this procedure lies well below unity even for complete dissociation. Across wide variations of carrier mobility and recombination strength it is a single-valued function of the fill factor and coincides with the short-circuit charge collection efficiency, reporting neither the generation yield nor anything about collection beyond what the fill factor already shows. Even for ideal transport the normalised photocurrent saturates below unity at an intensity-independent first-order limit set by recombination of photogenerated carriers with injected equilibrium charge. Applied to four organic solar cells whose generation efficiencies are known independently, the apparent dissociation probabilities track the short-circuit collection efficiency rather than the generation yield. We therefore suggest this construction not be used, particularly in the high-efficiency non-fullerene acceptor systems that are now state of the art.

papers.title: Spatially multiplexed opto-electronic Ising machine with single-shot parallel readout of 100,000 spins
papers.abstract: Ising machines offer a promising route to solving NP-hard combinatorial optimization problems by mapping them onto the ground state of the Ising model. Free-space optical implementations are attractive for their inherent parallelism, scalability, and energy efficiency, yet nearly all rely on individual, sequential spin updates, leaving most of this parallelism unexploited. Here, we reclaim it with a free-space optical analog Ising machine built from off-the-shelf components in which every spin is addressed in parallel and read out in a single camera shot, while letting the system evolve under analog dynamics rather than being written and read one spin at a time. We demonstrate this architecture with over 100,000 spins, the largest spatially multiplexed analog Ising machine reported to date, with a realistic path beyond one million spins limited only by spatial-light-modulator and camera resolution. Across sparse and dense MaxCut and fully connected number-partitioning instances, our machine matches state-of-the-art solution quality. Because every spin updates in parallel, throughput increases with system size, unlike time-multiplexed machines, which slow as problems grow. The same free-space geometry also lets us solve more than 50 problem instances simultaneously, further boosting throughput. Together, these results mark an important step towards a scalable, and energy-efficient Ising machine.

papers.title: Galvanometer Mirror Based Femtosecond-Laser Volumetric Displays
papers.abstract: Femtosecond-laser-induced plasma enables self-emissive voxels to be generated directly in air for drawing three-dimensional images. Galvanometer-mirror-based beam scanning provides a method for rapidly moving plasma voxels using a relatively simple optical configuration. However, the generated plasma voxels are not ideal points but luminous regions with finite lengths and widths. Variations in voxel shape and orientation caused by focusing and scanning conditions may therefore affect the appearance of rendered points and lines. Nevertheless, quantitative relationships between focusing and scanning conditions and plasma-voxel geometry remain insufficiently characterized in systems using a two-axis galvanometer mirror and a single focusing lens. Here, we quantitatively investigate how focal length and two-axis galvanometer scan angle affect the shape of plasma voxels and the projected inclination of their principal axes. For focal lengths ranging from 75 to 300 mm, the mean plasma length increased from 1.39 to 4.64 mm. These results indicate that increasing the focal length produces more elongated and anisotropic plasma voxels. The projected inclination of the plasma principal axis varied approximately linearly with the corresponding scan angle, although the response differed between the two scanning axes. These results provide quantitative design data for selecting focusing conditions and correcting voxel shape and orientation according to scanning conditions in galvanometer-mirror-based aerial volumetric displays.

papers.title: Sprouting Fields of Conducting Polymer Dendrites as Evolving Organic Electrochemical Frameworks to Interconnect Electrode Arrays
papers.abstract: Balancing high performance with sustainability in microelectronics is challenged by energy-intensive processes, scarce materials and limited recyclability. Inspired by nature, a promising solution relies on the evolution of the foundry model to transient microelectronics, using electrochemistry to grow adaptive circuits on demand and during operation. To this end, this study explores how to harness the morphogenesis of conducting polymer dendrites between stacks of micro-electrode arrays to dynamically interconnect them with voltage pulses. Using propylene carbonate as a solvent, we investigated the dynamics of the electroconvective growth of poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) (PEDOT), revealing strong structural dependencies between the morphology of the electrogenerated polymer and the confinement of the micro-electrodes. As the system evolves from 2D flat patterns to 3D dendritic structures, the capability of the conducting polymer to locally interconnect specific nodes heavily depends on the size and density of the arrays which directly impact the flow distribution during growth. By unraveling how a device geometry enables the growth of dendritic interconnections on integrated micro-electrode arrays, the morphogenesis of conducting polymer dendrites not only addresses the longstanding issue of heterogeneous integration in microelectronics, but also opens the way to a paradigm where electronic devices learn as they grow in our pockets.

papers.title: SOP Sensing in Hollow-Core Fiber: Forward Sensing using COTS Transponder and Localization with Coherent OTDR
papers.abstract: We experimentally investigate and compare distributed state-of-polarization sensing in support-tube hollow-core and standard single-mode fiber. Despite significantly weaker Rayleigh backscattering and reduced polarization sensitivity in hollow-core fiber, polarization perturbations remain observable and spatially localizable, demonstrating the feasibility of SOP-based distributed sensing in hollow-core fiber

papers.title: Composite Dielectric-Loaded Metallic Metagratings for Dual-Polarized Transmissive Beam Manipulation
papers.abstract: We present and experimentally demonstrate a comprehensive analytical suite for the design of transmissive metal-based metagratings (MGs) for dual-polarized anomalous refraction. Considering a composite configuration of perforated metallic slabs with controlled dielectric loading, we develop a rigorous mode-matching formulation tying the various MG degrees of freedom to the various reflected and transmitted Floquet-Bloch modes, enabling efficient beam deflection for both transverse electric (TE) and transverse magnetic (TM) polarizations. Inherently versatile, the analytical framework accurately models single-layer and double-layer constructs with multiple rectangular perforations per unit cell, each potentially loaded with dielectric material. We harness this degree-of-freedom abundance to devise diverse polarization-sensitive transmissive MGs, ranging from all-metallic single-layer and double-layer structures for single-polarized (TM or TE) perfect anomalous refraction, to dielectric-loaded architectures implementing dual-polarized routing of the incident wave. Beyond highlighting concrete paths to address TE-polarized fields in such formations, our results, validated via full-wave simulations and experiments at K band, showcase the great potential of metal-based MGs for manipulating fields in transmission, facilitating effective synthesis of durable dual-polarized beamforming superstrates for environmentally demanding and high power antenna applications.

papers.title: Monolithic ultraviolet-to- near infrared photodetection enabled by an aluminium oxide photonic platform
papers.abstract: Broadband photonic integrated circuits require waveguide platforms that combine low optical loss across a wide spectral range with integrated photodetection. Here we demonstrate a monolithically integrated atomic-layer-deposited (ALD) aluminium oxide (Al$_2$O$_3$)-on-silicon platform enabling waveguide-coupled photodetection from the ultraviolet to the near-infrared. The architecture employs evanescent coupling between low-loss Al$_2$O$_3$ waveguides and silicon p-i-n photodiodes. The platform supports photodetection at 375, 658 and 780 nm, extending integrated silicon photodetection into the ultraviolet. The devices exhibit linear photocurrent scaling with optical power, dark currents of approximately 2 pA at 50 V reverse bias and nanosecond-scale temporal response. We further demonstrate centimetre-scale ultraviolet Mach-Zehnder interferometer circuits with integrated photodiodes. The same detector architecture is implemented with Si$_3$N$_4$ waveguides, whereas the lower ultraviolet propagation loss of Al$_2$O$_3$ enables an approximately 15-fold higher photodetection response at 375 nm. These results establish ALD Al$_2$O$_3$ as a broadband integrated photonics platform for sensing, spectroscopy and quantum technologies.

papers.title: Atomic interferometry based on a phase-jump error signal with suppression of the lineshape-asymmetry-caused shift
papers.abstract: We develop a method for forming Ramsey fringes in atomic interferometers as a difference error signal using the phase-jump technique for Ramsey pulses (phase-jump error signal). In this case, the measurement procedure can be implemented as stabilization (locking) of the frequency chirp rate at the central zero of the error signal. We show analytically that this approach allows suppressing the lineshape-asymmetry-caused shift (LACS). This shift was recently theoretically predicted and experimentally identified in the papers [V. I. Yudin et al., JETP Lett. \textbf{122}, 737 (2025); D. N. Kapusta et al., JETP Lett. \textbf{123}, 388 (2026)]. A characteristic feature of the LACS is an inverse cubic dependence $\propto 1/T^3$ (where $T$ is the time between adjacent Ramsey pulses), and it can become dominant for interferometers with a short baseline. Therefore, the developed measurement algorithm with a phase-jump error signal will enable significant improvement in the metrological performance of compact quantum sensors for various purposes (atomic gravimeters, accelerometers, gyroscopes).

papers.title: Self-organized photonic time quasicrystal from a single imposed clock
papers.abstract: A photonic time crystal usually writes a clock into a medium. Here one clock does more than program the medium: it seeds a quasiperiodic temporal order that the nonlinear medium selects for itself. In a guided-wave lattice of nonlinear dipoles, a single-tone pump modulates the polarization sector, while Maxwell--polarization back-action selects two response frequencies whose only resolved low-order relation is the pump-locked sum condition. Their sum phase locks to the pump and the complementary phase winds, producing a photonic discrete time quasicrystal with torus-like phase dynamics and a discrete combination spectrum. Site-resolved measurements show locked-phase coherence across the measured lattice sites over a finite control-parameter window. These results establish a route from externally programmed time-varying media to self-organized temporal order in nonlinear photonic systems.

papers.title: Photonic processors that carry their own unclonable fingerprint
papers.abstract: Physically unclonable functions (PUFs) derive cryptographic keys from uncontrollable fabrication disorder, removing the need to store secrets in vulnerable non-volatile memory. Programmable photonic processors are natural candidates for PUFs, because each of their many tunable interferometers carries its own fabrication imperfections. However, we show that the mesh topology itself funnels light along short paths, so that most of this disorder contributes little to the response. Here we introduce an isotropic ring routing scheme that steers light to the core of a hexagonal mesh and redistributes it uniformly towards the perimeter, suppressing a distance-dependent power decay of 14.7 dB and raising the mean Shannon entropy of the response from 1.95 to 3.48 bits by reprogramming alone. Experiments on two independently fabricated 72-unit silicon processors show that a nominally identical device cannot reproduce the target's responses even after its passive phase profile is fully compensated. Combining isotropic routing with spectral readout yields 1107 bits per challenge, exceeding previous results by two orders of magnitude, with 49.8% inter-challenge and 50.0% inter-chip Hamming distances and a 4.9% intra-chip distance. These results establish general-purpose programmable photonic processors as reconfigurable, high-capacity hardware roots of trust.

papers.title: Dynamic distortion from discretized coupling feedback in soft-spin Ising machines
papers.abstract: Although Ising machines (IMs) have grown in popularity as physics-based accelerators for combinatorial optimization, most literature focuses on empirically obtained benchmarks with low universality. We propose dynamic feedback distortion as a universal, platform-agnostic metric for the effect of coupling field discretization in time-multiplexed IMs. Its closed form consists of a static offset and a harmonic series: a mid-tread coupling element (or a half-step bias) removes the former, and injected noise (dither) attenuates the latter. In a simulated optoelectronic IM, 2-bit mid-tread feedback with noise below half a quantization step solves a 50 spin M\"obius ladder in up to 99\% of runs. In a coherent IM, dithered 2-bit mid-tread feedback outperforms 4-bit mid-rise feedback on a M\"obius ladder and matches 4-bit feedback on 2D tiling problems. Triangular dither performs best when the spatial-frequency content of the ground state is unknown. These results show that reducing the static and harmonic components of the network distortion greatly increases the success rate of low-resolution quantized IMs.
